# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.

content:
1| import re
   2| 
   3| def slugify(text: str) -> str:
   4|     """Turn arbitrary text into a URL slug: lowercase, ASCII letters and
   5|     digits, words separated by single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphens."""
   6|     text = text.lower()
   7|     text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", text)
   8|     return text.strip("-")

The fix works. Both examples from the issue now produce the expected output:

- `slugify("Hello,  World!")` → `"hello-world"` (the `+` quantifier collapses consecutive non-alphanumerics into a single hyphen, and `strip("-")` removes the trailing one)
- `slugify("--a--b--")` → `"a-b"`

The public signature is unchanged, and the test suite passes (2 tests, OK).

arguments.summary: Fixed `slugify` in textkit/slug.py by changing the regex from `[^a-z0-9]` to `[^a-z0-9]+` so runs of non-alphanumeric characters collapse into a single hyphen, and added `.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens. This makes `slugify("Hello,  World!")` return `"hello-world"` and `slugify("--a--b--")` return `"a-b"`, with the public signature unchanged and all tests passing.
